AboutPage.title: About us
AboutPage.description: WhatAisle helps neighborhood grocery stores answer the question they hear most: “where is it?”
AboutPage.p1: WhatAisle is self-service product-finding software for neighborhood grocery stores. Shoppers scan a store QR code, ask where something is, and see the shelf with a map.
AboutPage.p2: Owners create their store page and draw the floor map online. Staff then select shelves and upload photos to keep product locations current, without typing product lists.
AboutPage.p3: Our customers are mostly overseas Chinese supermarkets, along with neighborhood markets of every kind. We build only what's useful, and make it work without a manual.
AboutPage.contactBody: Email us directly, or leave a message on the contact page — we answer both.

snap.title: Staff snap the shelves
snap.description: Staff take a few photos as they walk past a shelf. No product lists, no data entry. The system recognizes every product in the photo — packaging in English, Chinese, Korean, or Japanese — and blurs any faces automatically.

memory.description: The system remembers which shelf every product sits on. The more photos staff take, the more complete it gets — and the easier shoppers find things.

seo.title: “What aisle is it in?” — answered for every product
seo.intro1: Shoppers ask the same questions all day: “What aisle is the soy sauce in?” “Which shelf has the rice vinegar?” With WhatAisle they scan a QR code and ask — and the shelf number plus a marked map comes back in seconds, without waiting for staff.
seo.intro2: Create your store page and draw the floor map online. Staff select shelves and upload photos to build product locations, without spreadsheets. Shoppers use their browser, with nothing to install.

owners.title: For store owners
owners.p1: Staff snap shelf photos as they walk by. The system recognizes every product — packaging in English, Chinese, Korean, or Japanese — files it under the right shelf, and blurs faces automatically. The more photos, the better the answers.
owners.p2: Your dashboard shows what shoppers searched for and what they couldn't find. Products people want but you don't carry yet — that is your most direct buying signal.
owners.p3: “Where is it?” interrupts your staff dozens of times a day. When shoppers get the answer themselves, staff can stay on stocking and checkout.

shoppers.title: For shoppers
shoppers.p1: No app, no account. Scan, then type, speak, or take a photo. Ask “where's the soy sauce?” and the shelf number and map come back in seconds. If the store hasn't photographed a product yet, it says “not found yet” honestly instead of guessing.

multilingual.title: Built for multilingual neighborhood markets
multilingual.p1: Neighborhood markets serve shoppers in many languages. WhatAisle understands English and Chinese, handles pinyin and typos, and reads packaging in four scripts. A shopper can ask in Chinese about a product labeled in Korean and still get the right shelf.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does WhatAisle answer the aisle or the shelf?
faq.a1: The shelf. A typical answer is “Shelf B4, left side”, with that shelf marked in red on the map — much more precise than an aisle number.
faq.q2: How much work is it to set up?
faq.a2: After payment, choose your store name and web address, set a workspace password, and draw the floor map on your store page. Confirm the map with your password. Once photo upload is ready, staff select shelves and take or upload photos.
faq.q3: Do shoppers need to download anything?
faq.a3: No. The QR code opens right in the phone's browser. Nothing to install, for shoppers or staff.
faq.a4: Shoppers can ask in English or Chinese, by typing or speaking. On the shelf side, the system reads packaging in English, Chinese, Korean, and Japanese.
faq.q5: What happens when a search finds nothing?
faq.a5: The shopper sees an honest “not found yet” plus close alternatives. You see the miss in your dashboard — either a reminder to photograph that shelf, or a product worth stocking.
faq.a6: Yes. Faces are blurred before shelf photos are saved, shopper photos are only used to recognize the product and are not kept, and searches are only viewed as totals, never tied to a person.
faq.a7: The standard price is US$199 for one month or US$1,999 for twelve months, before tax. Annual billing saves US$389 compared with twelve monthly payments. You can cancel future renewals anytime. See the pricing page for details.

seo.outro: Don't let shoppers wander the store, and don't make staff walk them there every time. Print one QR poster and have staff start photographing shelves today.
